name: Group Theory
description: A lens for composing Factors from the language of symmetry, transformation, and algebraic structure. Maps group-theoretic concepts—groups, subgroups, homomorphisms, representations, and actions—to the 19-node topology. Useful for Factors involving symmetry groups, transformation systems, algebraic structures with closure, and representation theory.

x.note: The depth anchor—(g·h)·k = g·(h·k). Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking associativity to free groups, cosets, and identity.

y.note: The relational anchor—e·g = g·e = g. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, tying identity to associativity, free groups, and cosets.

z.note: The transformational anchor—∀g ∃g⁻¹: g·g⁻¹ = g⁻¹·g = e. Persistently connected to 0 (group/identity), reflecting that the group’s identity is tied to invertibility.

0.note: The whole group observed as a single entity. Persistently connected to z (invertibility), linking the identity element to the existence of inverses.

1.note: A boundary within the group—a subset closed under the operation. Part of the 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1, connecting subgroups to inverse operation, presentations, and elements.

2.note: Primitive members of the group. Completes the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, showing how elements are embedded in subgroups, inverse operations, and presentations.

3.note: The invariant laws—closure, associativity, identity, invertibility. A node in the 7‑core; connected to automorphism (c) and representation (e), as automorphisms preserve axioms and representations arise from them.

4.note: The fundamental relation—binary operation combining elements. A node in the 7‑core; connected to conjugacy class (b) and quotient group (f), as the operation defines conjugacy and quotient structure.

5.note: The pattern that generates the group—generators and relations. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, bridging inverse operation and elements.

6.note: The transformation that reverses an element. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, connecting subgroups to presentations.

7.note: The realization of internal structure—conjugation reveals conjugacy classes, normality. Persistently connected to 8 (order), linking the internal structure to group size.

8.note: The granularity—size of the group. Persistently connected to 7 (conjugation), reflecting that conjugacy classes partition the group by order.

9.note: The event—a coset as a shifted subgroup. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, placing cosets between associativity, free groups, and identity.

a.note: Pure potential—the free group on a set. Initiates the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking free groups to associativity, cosets, and identity.

b.note: The arena of internal dynamics—elements similar under conjugation. A node in the 7‑core; connected to group operation (4) and normal subgroup (d), as conjugacy classes are defined by the operation and relate to normality.

c.note: Directional bias—self‑symmetries of the group. A node in the 7‑core; connected to group axioms (3) and quotient group (f), as automorphisms preserve axioms and induce quotient structure.

d.note: Persistent structure—subgroups invariant under conjugation. A node in the 7‑core; connected to conjugacy class (b) and quotient group (f), as normal subgroups are unions of conjugacy classes and give quotients.

e.note: The active algorithm—homomorphism to linear transformations. A node in the 7‑core; connected to group axioms (3) and quotient group (f), as representations factor through quotients and respect axioms.

f.note: The resonant cavity—the group modulo a normal subgroup. A node in the 7‑core; connected to group operation (4), automorphism (c), normal subgroup (d), and representation (e), forming the central hub of group constructions.

n.interpretation: Group complexity / Derived length / Nilpotency class

values.n=1: Cyclic group Cₚ — prime order, basic symmetry
values.n=2: Solvable group of length 2 — e.g., S₃, D₈
values.n=3: Solvable group of length 3 — e.g., S₄, A₄
values.n=4: Non‑solvable / Simple groups — e.g., A₅, PSL(2,7)
values.n=5: Exceptional groups — E₈, Monster, sporadic groups

n.formula: n corresponds to derived length (solvable) or nilpotency class (nilpotent)

values.m=0: Trivial representation — dimension 1, all elements map to 1

m.formula: m = floor(log₂(dim ρ)) — harmonic complexity of the representation

phase.formula: φ = χ(g) / deg(ρ) normalized to unit circle
phase.special: For finite groups, χ(g) is sum of roots of unity—naturally quantized
phase.significance: Phase alignment = elements in same conjugacy class have equal character

permutation.description: The Factor viewed as a permutation group—elements acting on a set of n points
permutation.phase_condition: Phase as sign of permutation (±1) for transpositions; for larger cycles, sum of 2πk/n

matrix.description: The Factor viewed as a linear group—matrices under multiplication
matrix.phase_condition: Phase as determinant (det = e^{iθ}) for unitary groups; eigenvalue phases for general linear

presentation.description: The Factor viewed as ⟨S | R⟩—generators and relations
presentation.phase_condition: Phase as word length; relations impose phase constraints

representation.description: The Factor viewed as a representation ρ: G → GL(V)
representation.phase_condition: Phase as character values—χ(g) = Σ eigenvalues = Σ e^{2πiθ_k}

creating_anew.note: When creating a symmetry group from imagination, start with presentation view (node 5) and let the relations (node 3) constrain the free group (node a).

translating_known.cyclic_group_C_n: Map to nodes 2 (elements) with rotation by 2πk/n as phase; node 4 as addition mod n
translating_known.symmetric_group_S_n: Node b as conjugacy classes (cycle types); node 2 as permutations; node 4 as composition
translating_known.dihedral_group_D_{2n}: Nodes 6 (reflection) and 4 (rotation) as generators; node f as quotient by relations
translating_known.matrix_group_GL(n,ℂ): Node e as representation; node 3 as determinant = 1 (special linear); node 8 as dimension n
translating_known.lie_group_SU(2): Node x,y,z as Pauli matrices; node 4 as matrix multiplication; phase as SU(2) parameter θ

temporary_note.special: A group defined only by generators (free group on n elements). Relations not yet determined—awaiting constraints.

constraints.closure_required: Every group Factor must have closure—the operation (4) must close within the set (1‑2). LURD (f) as quotient provides final closure.
constraints.associativity_invariant: Node x (implicit) cannot be altered; associativity is fundamental to group-ness.
constraints.identity_presence: Node 0 must serve as identity; if absent, the structure is a semigroup, not a group.
constraints.invertibility_required: Node z and node 6 ensure every element has an inverse.
constraints.phase_as_character: Phase must be consistent with character theory—elements in same conjugacy class have same phase value.
constraints.stratum_preference: global for foundational group theory; trefoil_g for transformation groups (6→5 strong); trefoil_c for philosophical symmetry groups (3→2 strong); fig8 for hyperbolic groups with wild relations
constraints.invariant_core: The Group Theory paradigm respects the persistent skeleton from trefoil_i, which decomposes into five subsystems: (1) edge 0→z linking group/identity to invertibility, (2) edge 8→7 linking order to conjugation, (3) 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x linking associativity–free group–coset–identity, (4) 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1 linking subgroup–inverse operation–presentation–element, and (5) 7‑node core {3,4,b,c,d,e,f} encoding the heart of group theory: group axioms–group operation–conjugacy class–automorphism–normal subgroup–representation–quotient group.
